steps.say: Scientists sort animals into groups by their features. One big question is whether an animal has a backbone.
Animals with a backbone are vertebrates. There are five groups: fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals.

figure.alt: One example of each vertebrate group: a fish, a frog (amphibian), a lizard (reptile), a bird and a cat (mammal).

steps.say: Fish have gills and scales. Amphibians have moist skin, and their young usually live in water.
Reptiles have dry, scaly skin. Birds have feathers, and mammals have hair and feed their young on milk.
Animals without a backbone are invertebrates. Insects, spiders, snails, worms and crabs are all invertebrates.

figure.alt: Five invertebrates: an ant (insect), a spider, a snail, a worm and a crab.

steps.say: Insects have six legs and three body parts. Spiders have eight legs and two body parts.

check.prompt: A dolphin breathes air and feeds its young on milk. Which group is it in?

options.why: Fish breathe with gills. Dolphins breathe air with lungs.
Amphibians have moist skin, and their young start life in water with gills.
Reptiles have dry, scaly skin, and most lay eggs.

hints: Living in water does not make an animal a fish.
Feeding young on milk is a feature of one group only.
Name the group whose mothers feed their babies on milk.
check.explanation: Dolphins breathe air and feed their young on milk, so they are mammals, even though they live in the sea.

options.why: A frog has a backbone, so it is a vertebrate. It is an amphibian.
An eagle has a backbone. It is a bird.
A shark has a backbone made of cartilage. It is a fish.

hints: Think about which animal has a soft body with no bones.
Cross out the animals that are fish, amphibians or birds.
check.explanation: A snail has a soft body and no backbone, so it is an invertebrate. Frogs, eagles and sharks are vertebrates.
